blockdesc-buckingmill-frame-*: The frame of a mechanically powered pair of drag saws that cross-cut tree trunks into logs. Fit two saw sashes, a crankshaft, feed levers and two blade kits to assemble it.
error-need-sash: Each blade kit goes into a saw sash. Fit another sash first.
error-blades-fitted: Both blade kits are already fitted.
error-blade-metal: Both blade kits must be the same metal. This mill has {0} blades.
error-not-a-part: That is not a part of this mill.
error-trunk-cut: The trunk is cut too far to take out.
error-no-logging: This mill cannot work with the installed Logging Expanded.
error-incomplete: Assemble the mill before loading a trunk.
error-bed-full: There is already a trunk in the mill.
error-saws-not-up: Wait for the saws to come up.
info-committed: Too far cut to take the trunk out
info-attop: Saws at the top: a trunk can go on now
info-nopower: Not turning fast enough, connect a turning axle
handbook-assembly-text: Place the frame where the whole machine has room: it is six blocks long, three wide and four high, and runs away from you, with the block you place as the middle of its near end. The far end takes the axle and the trunks; the logs come out of the near end. Then fit Immersive Woodworking's sawmill parts with rightmouse, in any order: two saw sashes, a crankshaft, feed levers and two blade kits of the same metal. Each blade kit goes into a sash, so fit a sash before each kit. No carriage is needed. The crankshaft strokes the two saws back and forth across the trunk, and they sink through it under their own weight. When they reach the bottom they trip the levers, which engage a windlass that winds them back up on ropes; at the top the carriage trips the levers back, the windlass lets go, and they start down again. While it is turning the mill never stops: with no trunk on the bed the saws keep going up and down. ctrl + rightmouse takes a blade kit back out. The other parts come back only when you break the frame, which drops every fitted part.
handbook-power-text: Connect a turning axle to the far end of the mill, high up, where the shaft ends (the top of the end, in the middle). The assembled mill is a heavy load, twice a plank sawmill's, and it only cuts while its shaft turns at a fair speed. Until it is assembled it barely loads the shaft.
handbook-trunks-text: The mill cuts Logging Expanded tree trunks of any size, one at a time. Trunks must have their branches removed first while Logging Expanded asks for that. Load a trunk with rightmouse, holding it, or with an empty hand to take one from your hotbar or backpack, while the saws are at the top of their cycle (the mill's info says when). A trunk storage rack standing on the ground against the mill's far end, under the axle, where trunks slide in lengthwise along the bed's rails, feeds the running mill: it takes the rack's top trunk whenever the bed is empty and the saws come round to the top. A branched trunk on top of the rack holds the line until you deal with it. ctrl + rightmouse takes the trunk back out, but only before a quarter of it is cut.
handbook-yield-text:
Every log stored in a trunk takes 8 turns of the shaft and gives 2 logs of its wood, which slide off the rails at the near end. A cut trunk's resin and branches are lost, as on a sawhorse.

After each cut the saws wind back up to the top, which takes 6 turns of the shaft from the bottom; with no trunk they take another 6 to come down, so an empty cycle is 12 turns. A trunk taken back out early lets them carry on down from where they are. The next trunk can only go on while they are at the top.

Each blade kit loses 1 durability for every 4 logs stored in a cut trunk, rounded up. A worn out kit breaks and the mill stops, its saws where they are, until a new one is fitted. These figures are the defaults of ModConfig/buckingsawmill.json.
